sources.news_title: Musk's Independent Campaign Committee Begins Spending Funds to Help the Republican Party in Midterm Elections
sources.text:
El comité independiente de campaña de Elon Musk reveló sus primeros gastos en favor de candidatos republicanos, donde destinó aproximadamente US$ 800.000 para ayudar a aspirantes al Congreso en varios estados, según muestran nuevos documentos presentados.
Los gastos del comité independiente de campaña, realizados en agosto y comunicados la noche de este miércoles, hora local, a la Comisión Federal de Elecciones, cubren costos de impresión, lo que indica que la operación política de Musk se centra en llegar directamente a los votantes. La inversión incluye ayuda para candidatos que compiten en contiendas senatoriales de alto perfil desde Maine hasta Texas.
La mayor parte del gasto recién revelado —más de US$ 247.000— se destinó a apoyar al candidato republicano al Senado Ken Paxton, fiscal general de Texas, quien ha sido ampliamente superado en gasto publicitario televisivo por el nominado demócrata de Texas, James Talarico. En las últimas semanas, la cuenta del comité independiente de campaña (America PAC) en X dirigió sus ataques contra Talarico, argumentando que sus posturas están desconectadas de los votantes de Texas.
Musk, la persona más rica del mundo, ya figura entre los mayores financiadores de las intermedias, con una inversión de más de US$ 50 millones en su Comité independiente de campaña y US$ 10 millones en donaciones a cada uno de los principales republicanos activos en su comité en las contiendas para la Cámara de Representantes y el Senado. También donó US$ 10 millones a un comité de campaña activo en la carrera por el Senado en Kentucky.
Otras contiendas donde el comité independiente de campaña de Musk ha realizado inversiones iniciales incluyen las elecciones al Senado en Iowa, Nueva Hampshire, Michigan y Ohio, así como carreras clave para la Cámara de Representantes en Nueva Jersey, Nueva York, Pensilvania y Virginia.
Esta actividad marca el regreso de Musk a la política republicana, más de un año después de haber protagonizado una disputa pública con el presidente Donald Trump. En un momento dado, amenazó con fundar su propio partido político, antes de abandonar esos planes y reconciliarse con Trump.
El comité se comprometió a ayudar a los republicanos a conservar sus mayorías en la Cámara y el Senado durante las elecciones intermedias de noviembre, destinando fondos tanto para defender escaños republicanos como para ganar distritos actualmente en manos de los demócratas, según una fuente familiarizada con los planes del comité.

sources.news_title: Elon Musk wades into Maine’s Senate race • Maine Morning Star
sources.text:
Republican U.S. Sen. Susan Collins of Maine tours the Maine Energy Marketers Association Technical Education Center in Brunswick on Sept. 3, 2026. (Photo by Emma Davis/ Maine Morning Star)
A Republican consulting firm working to reelect Susan Collins received the second largest share of spending from Elon Musk’s super PAC last month.
America PAC has spent just over $170,000 in Maine’s U.S. Senate race, which Democrats view as a key pickup opportunity to gain control of the upper chamber. Overall, a Federal Election Commission disclosure released Wednesday showed the super PAC spent over $800,000 last month on races with Republican incumbents and candidates in competitive districts.
“First of all, I wasn’t aware of that donation,” Collins told reporters in Brunswick on Thursday. “I knew he was going to get involved in political campaigns, but I had not heard that there was a specific donation.”
The August disclosures reveal what are expected to be the first in a series of donations from Musk, the world’s richest person, who has reportedly authorized his super PAC to spend $100 million to $120 million to help elect Republicans in November, two unnamed sources told the New York Times this summer.
Red Maverick Media LLC, the primary direct mail vendor for Collins based in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, received four separate donations dedicated to Maine’s Senate race from America PAC in late August.
Texas’ Senate race between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico received the most money from Musk’s PAC, around $248,000, followed by Ohio ($105,675), New Hampshire ($91,458.50), Iowa ($54,600), Michigan ($25,605) and Alaska ($17,235).
Speaking of Musk’s time leading the Department of Government Efficiency at the start of President Donald Trump’s second term, Collins said on Thursday, “I don’t agree with him on everything, but I do agree with him that we need to eliminate waste and be much more efficient in government.”
On that note, Collins called the reports of fraud in Maine’s Medicaid system “absolutely unacceptable.” Vice President JD Vance and Mehmet Oz, administrator of the U.S. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, on separate visits to Maine have expressed similar concerns.
The Maine Department of Health and Human Services has disputed claims that the agency is not cracking down on fraud, announcing earlier this month that it suspended payments to five providers and terminated two providers’ contracts for subjecting residents to serious health risks and unsafe conditions.

sources.news_title: Susan Collins Confronted About Elon Musk Donation: ‘I Wasn’t Aware of That’
Elon Musk is throwing his cash around in Pa. again. This time, in support of 3 GOP lawmakers in swing districts
Elon Musk is throwing his cash around in Pa. again. This time, in support of three GOP lawmakers in swing districts.
sources.text:
Elon Musk is throwing his cash around in Pa. again. This time, in support of three GOP lawmakers in swing districts.
Elon Musk's super PAC has contributed roughly $12,000 a piece to benefit GOP U.S. Reps. Ryan Mackenzie, Rob Bresnahan, and Scott Perry.
Elon Musk is back.
The richest man in the world, who was laser-focused on delivering Pennsylvania for President Donald Trump in 2024, is wielding his wallet in the Keystone State once again to support Republicans in three swing congressional districts ahead of the midterms.
America PAC, Musk’s super PAC, has contributed roughly $12,000 apiece in support of U.S. Reps. Ryan Mackenzie, of Lehigh; Rob Bresnahan, of Lackawanna; and Scott Perry, of York — all GOP incumbents facing tough reelection challenges, according to an independent expenditure report filed Wednesday.
Though small potatoes in comparison, America PAC’s contributions in Pa. come roughly two years after Musk launched his intense and unprecedented efforts to mobilize voters in Pennsylvania for Trump when he spent millions of dollars, hosted a disinformation-filled town hall in Delaware County, and offered $1 million to random voters who signed a petition from his super PAC.
Republicans lauded Musk for the energy and clout he brought to the campaign trail and it earned him a place in Trump’s inner circle at the time, leading to his turbulent tenure overseeing the Department of Government Efficiency.
The PAC’s contributions for the congressional races went toward printing at Storytellers Group LLC, a Tennessee-based company, according to the report. He also contributed to several other competitive races across the country.
Even though Musk is not yet deeply involved in Pennsylvania, the PAC’s spending signifies that the billionaire likely views these three congressional seats as important as both parties vie for control of the U.S. House.
America PAC and spokespersons for Mackenzie, Bresnahan, and Perry did not immediately return a request for comment.
The PAC also has yet to make a contribution in support of U.S. Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R., Bucks) will also be defending his seat against Democratic challenger Bob Harvie in a swing district this November.
The Bucks County Republican already has a massive war chest of his own, far surpassing his GOP counterparts in total fundraising.
“I think Fitzpatrick is fairly well positioned regardless of what Mr. Musk does or does not do,” said Christopher Nicholas, a GOP consultant.
But the three GOP incumbents benefiting from Musk’s latest spending all lagged their Democratic challengers in fundraising during the most recent quarter. And Tesla and SpaceX’s CEO’s support could help close the gap.
Musk has become a figure of scorn for Pennsylvania Democrats, and the challengers of Mackenzie, Bresnahan, and Perry all criticized his involvement in their respective races.
Bob Brooks, a retired firefighter and union leader who is challenging Mackenzie, seen as one of the most vulnerable incumbents in the nation, said in a statement that Musk is “spending a fortune to buy this congressional seat” in the Lehigh Valley.
“I have a message for Elon and Ryan: Pennsylvania’s Seventh district is not for sale,” he said.
A spokesperson for former TV news anchor Janelle Stelson, who is running in a rematch against Perry in the 10th District, said that: “Scott Perry lacks the courage to highlight Musk’s efforts to increase corruption in our government, so now Musk is rewarding Perry for his subservience.”
And in the 8th Congressional District, Scranton Mayor Paige Cognetti said: “Unlike Rob, I don’t take a dime of corporate PAC money.”
“In Congress, I’ll answer to the people of NEPA, and no one else,” she said.
Staff Writer Sam Janesch contributed reporting.

sources.news_title: Elon Musk’s America PAC spends $800,000 to boost Republicans in key midterm races
sources.text:
Elon Musk’s super PAC, America PAC, has spent about $800,000 in battleground races to support Republican candidates as the 2026 US midterm elections approach, according to NBC News.
The PAC is targeting several closely contested Senate races, including contests in Maine, Michigan and Texas, the news outlet reported, citing a campaign finance filing submitted to the Federal Election Commission on Wednesday night.
America PAC disclosed nearly $250,000 in recent spending in the Texas Senate race, more than $170,000 in Maine and more than $25,000 in Michigan, according to the filing.
The spending comes roughly two months before the midterm elections, with Democrats seeking to flip competitive seats and regain control of one or both chambers of Congress. NBC News reported that the latest filing suggests Musk is prepared to deploy additional funds as the midterm campaign intensifies.
America PAC is also spending in House and Senate contests across more than a dozen states, including Alaska, Florida, Iowa, Maine, Michigan, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, Virginia and Wisconsin, NBC News reported.
The spending in Texas is relatively modest compared with the tens of millions of dollars expected to be spent in the race between Republican Ken Paxton and Democratic state Rep. James Talarico. However, the spending comes as Republicans have raised concerns about Paxton’s fundraising gap and urged outside groups to help bolster the GOP nominee.
Andrew Romeo, a spokesperson for America PAC, said in a statement earlier this summer that the group was “excited to again be part of the team” supporting Republican candidates in the midterms.
“The president’s political team and the rest of the GOP apparatus have built a top-notch operation” to help Republicans retain control of Congress, Romeo said, according to the news outlet.
Musk emerged as one of the biggest financial backers of Republicans during the 2024 presidential campaign. He spent more than $250 million supporting Donald Trump and other Republican candidates.
The billionaire continued his political involvement the following year, spending millions to support a conservative candidate in a Wisconsin Supreme Court race. That candidate ultimately lost.
Musk and Trump initially developed a close political relationship during the early months of Trump's second presidential term. Musk served as the public face of the so-called Department of Government Efficiency, appearing at Cabinet meetings and gaining significant access to the president.
Their relationship later deteriorated, with Musk publicly clashing with Trump and briefly floating the idea of creating a new political party called the “America Party.”
The feud, however, appears to have cooled. Musk and Trump have since been seen together, including during Trump's state visit to China earlier this year.
With the 2026 midterms approaching, Musk’s renewed PAC spending could make him an important source of outside financial support for Republican candidates in some of the country's most competitive races.

sources.news_title: Musk’s Midterms Play: Ken Paxton, Socialist Scaremongering
sources.text:
Elon Musk declared last year that he was going to do “a lot less” political spending in the future, adding that if he felt compelled to invest more of his (unfathomable amounts of) money, he would. But he did not “currently see a reason.” Well apparently he’s got one now, and it generally falls under the motivation of keeping Republicans in power come November.
Late on Wednesday, Musk’s super-PAC revealed that it spent approximately $800,000 last month on key House and Senate races with the most significant amounts of money going to Texas and Maine. In Texas, where Democrat James Talarico holds a slim lead over Attorney General Ken Paxton — whom the conservative National Review recently described as “spectacularly corrupt” and “vaguely amphibious-looking” — Musk’s PAC spent $247,595. Trump’s endorsement of Paxton has hardly been ringing. “You might not like the way he dresses,” “the way he looks,” or “his television interviews,” Trump said on Wednesday. “But he was the best attorney general [and] that speaks a lot louder than the suit he’s wearing that doesn’t look so great.”
In Maine — where Susan Collins, the second-most unpopular senator in the country is facing a challenge from Democrat Troy Jackson — the America PAC wrote a check for $170,224.29. Money also went to Ohio ($105,675), New Hampshire ($91,458), Iowa ($54,600), Michigan ($25,605) and Alaska ($17,235). Disclosures show over $207,000 in spending on digital ads, including one featuring NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani that warned people: “You couldn’t vote in his election, and socialism declared victory over America’s biggest city. If you don’t vote in November, socialism could declare victory over America.”
The $800,000 August spend is of course far from the total amount Musk is expected to pour into the midterms, having reportedly authorized his PAC to spend $100 million to $120 million to defeat the Democratic Party. That itself represents less than half of what the SpaceX founder contributed to get Donald Trump elected in 2024 before he took a job in the White House decimating the federal government.
Musk is just one of a number of billionaires injecting giant sums of money into House and Senate races in the hopes of keeping Congress under GOP control. Citadel founder Ken Griffin has also donated some $40 million to midterm races and may ultimately donate roughly twice that by November, according to a report from The Wall Street Journal. In August, the Washington Post reported that major Republican-supporting donors have outspent those supporting Democrats by nearly three to one with $880 million going toward GOP candidates and a relatively paltry $290 million for Democrats.

sources.news_title: Elon Musk’s super PAC starts spending to help GOP in midterms, including Texas’ Ken Paxton
sources.text:
Elon Musk’s super PAC has disclosed its first spending on behalf of Republican candidates, providing roughly $800,000 to help congressional contenders across several states, new filings show.
The expenditures by America PAC, made in August and disclosed on Wednesday night to the Federal Election Commission, cover printing costs – a sign that Musk’s political operation is focused on direct voter outreach. The spending includes help for candidates competing in high-profile Senate races from Maine to Texas.
The largest share of the newly disclosed spending, more than $247,000, went to aid Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general who has been vastly outspent on the airwaves by Texas’ Democratic nominee James Talarico. In recent weeks, America PAC’s feed on X has targeted Talarico, arguing that his views are out of touch with Texas voters.
Musk, the world’s richest person, already is one of the biggest funders in the midterm elections, plowing more than $50 million into his America PAC and donating $10 million each to the main Republican super PACs active in House and Senate races. He also has given $10 million to a super PAC active in Kentucky’s Senate race.
Other races where America PAC has made early investments include Senate contests in Iowa, New Hampshire, Michigan and Ohio and key House races in New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania and Virginia.
The activity marks a reengagement in Republican politics for Musk more than a year after he publicly bickered with President Donald Trump. At one point, he threatened to start his own political party before abandoning those plans and reconciling with Trump.
The PAC has committed to helping Republicans retain their House and Senate majorities in November’s midterm elections, spending both to defend Republican-held seats and pick up districts now held by Democrats, according to a source familiar with the committee’s plans.

sources.news_title: Musk’s America PAC spends about $800K in key midterm races
Elon Musk starts spending his midterm election millions, revealing his key Senate targets
sources.text:
Elon Musk's super PAC is putting its first midterm money behind some of the GOP's most important election battlegrounds, spending more than $800,000 across seven Senate races and a handful of competitive House districts, according to a new Federal Election Commission disclosure.
The spending by America PAC offers the clearest look yet at where the Tesla and SpaceX CEO is directing his political operation, after the billionaire who previously supported Democrats reportedly authorized the group to spend as much as $120 million on an effort to help elect Republicans this November.
Nearly 90% of the $800,475 disclosed Wednesday night went toward Senate races, with the largest share — more than $247,000 — spent in Texas to support Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton and oppose Democrat James Talarico in an increasingly competitive contest.
Paxton has struggled to keep pace with Talarico's spending. As of Aug. 20, Talarico's campaign had spent more than $25 million on advertising since the general election began in late May, compared with just $119,000 by Paxton's campaign, according to AdImpact data cited by the Texas Tribune.
America PAC had been increasingly targeting Talarico on social media before the newly disclosed expenditures.
The group also spent about $170,000 in Maine, where Republican Sen. Susan Collins is seeking reelection, and nearly $106,000 in Ohio to support Republican Sen. Jon Husted. The PAC disclosed another $91,459 in New Hampshire, $54,600 in Iowa, $25,605 in Michigan and $17,235 in Alaska.
The expenditures were made between Aug. 18 and Aug. 31, with the disclosure also listing two expenditures scheduled for Sept. 10. All were categorized as printing expenses, indicating the money was being used for mail advertising.
America PAC spent much less on House races, which are usually cheaper than statewide races, directing nearly $90,000 across eight contests. The spending benefited Republican Reps. Derrick Van Orden of Wisconsin, Mike Lawler of New York, Jen Kiggans of Virginia, Tom Kean Jr. of New Jersey, and Scott Perry, Rob Bresnahan and Ryan Mackenzie of Pennsylvania, as well as Republican Scott Singer, who is challenging Democratic Rep. Jared Moskowitz in Florida.
The spending was disclosed days after House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., reportedly met with Musk in Texas while campaigning for Republicans in competitive congressional races. Johnson later told House Republican leaders about the meeting but did not say whether Musk had made any commitments about midterm spending.
"He's made public a lot of what he's doing," Johnson said to CBS News when asked about Musk's plans. "I'm not going to talk about our conversation on that point, but we're going to win the midterms."
Johnson did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNBC.
Musk spent hundreds of millions of dollars supporting President Donald Trump and other Republican candidates in 2024, including more than $239 million given to America PAC. But he later appeared ready to retreat from that level of political involvement after joining the Trump administration to lead the Department of Government Efficiency, then having a public falling out with the president.
Asked last year whether he intended to continue spending at the same pace, Musk said he planned to spend "a lot less" on politics.
"I think I've done enough," Musk said.
But Musk has since repaired his relationship with Trump and Republican leaders. The New York Times reported in July that Musk had authorized America PAC to spend up to $120 million on a field program aimed at electing Republicans this November.
The latest expenditures are still just a fraction of that potential commitment.
They also come before America PAC has disclosed the latest influx of money financing its midterm push. FEC data covering the 2025-26 election cycle through June 30 show America PAC had raised $50.3 million and spent $52.3 million, leaving it with about $274,000 in cash on hand.

Elon Musk’s super PAC has funneled about $800,000 into battleground races across the country to boost Republican candidates.
Musk’s America PAC is weighing in on highly competitive races, including the Senate contests in Maine, Michigan and Texas, according to a report it filed with the Federal Election Commission on Wednesday night.
America PAC disclosed nearly a quarter-million dollars in recent spending on the Texas Senate race, more than $170,000 on the Maine Senate race and more than $25,000 on the Michigan Senate race.
NBC News last week reported that the super PAC had started to spend on digital ads in Maine, Michigan and New Hampshire to support conservatives and compel people to register to vote.
The new filing indicates that the billionaire is prepared to unleash more money as Democrats and Republicans barrel toward midterm elections, which are just about two months away. Democrats are seeking to flip several competitive seats in hopes of retaking one or both chambers of Congress.
And the spending in Texas’ Senate race, although small when compared to the tens of millions expected to rain down in the contest between Paxton and Democratic state Rep. James Talarico, comes as Republicans have raised concerns about the their nominee’s fundraising gap and called on outside groups to help fill it.
Musk’s super PAC is spending money across the country in House and Senate races in more than a dozen states: Alaska, Florida, Iowa, Maine, Michigan, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, Virginia and Wisconsin.
Andrew Romeo, a spokesperson for America PAC, said in a statement over the summer that it was “excited to again be part of the team” to support Republicans’ midterm efforts.
“The president’s political team and the rest of the GOP apparatus have built a top-notch operation that will put Republicans in a strong position to buck history and retain control of Congress this fall, and we’re excited to again be part of the team,” he said in the prior statement.
Musk was a major financial player in the 2024 presidential race, when he spent more than $250 million to support President Donald Trump and Republicans. The next year, he spent millions of dollars to boost a conservative Wisconsin Supreme Court candidate, who lost the race.
Trump and Musk had a close relationship in the first months of the president’s second term, when Musk headed the so-called Department of Government Efficiency. Musk made appearances at cabinet meetings, and he appeared to have the president’s ear.
The two had a brief, but contentious, falling out. Musk briefly threatened to create a third political party — the “America Party” — amid his frustration with Trump, but has not followed through.
The two men have since appeared to be on good terms. Earlier this year, Musk traveled with Trump to China for the president’s state visit.

sources.news_title: Elon Musk's Super PAC Targets Competitive Senate Races as $100 Million Republican Push Gets Underway
sources.text:
Elon Musk's super PAC spent more than $800,000 in August supporting Republican candidates in competitive congressional races, the first disclosed spending from a midterm effort that could ultimately exceed $100 million despite Musk's previous statements that he intended to reduce his political involvement.
Federal Election Commission filings released Wednesday show America PAC directed most of the money toward Senate contests, including nearly $248,000 in Texas, $170,000 in Maine and $106,000 in Ohio. The group also spent in New Hampshire, Iowa, Michigan and Alaska, as well as competitive House districts in several states.
The expenditures were categorized as printing costs, suggesting they funded political mailers. Separately, America PAC has spent more than $207,000 on digital advertising in Texas, Michigan, New Hampshire and Maine, according to AdImpact and Facebook advertising records.
The spending follows The New York Times' July report that Musk authorized America PAC to spend between $100 million and $120 million on a field operation aimed at helping Republicans in at least eight states. The effort is expected to target competitive Senate and House races and include firms focused on turning out voters.
The investment marks a return to Republican politics for Musk after his public falling-out with President Donald Trump last year and threats to create a third party. Musk spent close to $300 million during the 2024 election cycle and was the largest individual political donor of either party, according to federal filings.
His renewed spending also contrasts with his recent public comments about stepping away from politics. "I think I got a little too involved in politics," Musk told The Economist in an interview published July 23. "I got carried away, frankly."
Musk is not currently expected to take as public a role in the midterms as he did during the 2024 presidential campaign. But America PAC's August expenditures indicate that the financial operation behind his political involvement is already underway.

sources.news_title: Elon Musk’s America PAC enters the 2026 midterm elections, spending over $800K on campaigns
sources.text:
Recent election filings and financial disclosures showed that Elon Musk’s America PAC has spent over $800,000 on political campaign materials for multiple congressional races in the 2026 midterm elections.
The total amount revealed to have been spent by America PAC on the congressional campaigns, as of Sept. 3, was $800,475.74. There were 44 separate expenditures listed in the filing with the Federal Election Commission, with expenditures ranging from as little as $500, such as that for the campaign of Rep. Thomas Kean, Jr. (R-NJ), to as much as $123,000 on the campaign of Republican senate candidate for Texas, Ken Paxton, and another $123,000 for campaign materials opposing Paxton’s Democratic opponent James Talarico.

The filings also show contributions for campaign materials supporting Republican Senate candidate for Michigan, Mike Rogers, Rep. Ashley Hinson’s (R-IA) Senate campaign, and Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY). They also revealed contributions for campaign materials opposing several Democratic candidates, including Cait Conley, Lawler’s opponent in New York’s 17th Congressional District, Rebecca Bennet, Kean’s opponent in New Jersey’s 7th Congressional District, Joshua Turek, Hinson’s opponent in Iowa, and Abdul el Sayed, Rogers’s opponent in Michigan.

Musk created America PAC during the 2024 election campaign season. The PAC’s stated purpose is to support the “key values” of a fair justice system, free speech, safe cities, secure borders, self-protection, and sensible spending. During the 2024 presidential election, the PAC paid volunteers for each voter who signed a petition supporting the First and Second Amendments. The PAC also awarded $1 million to several volunteers collecting petition signatures.
America PAC came under fire for several reasons during and after the election. Democrats throughout the country alleged that Musk’s PAC was illegal and called for legal action against it and its shutdown. After the election, the PAC was sued by volunteers who had collected signatures for the petition but had yet to receive their promised payments.

sources.news_title: Elon Musk's Super PAC Dumped $800K Into Battleground Races in August
sources.text:
Tech billionaire Elon Musk’s super PAC spent around $800,000 on House and Senate candidates in battleground states last month, according to a new disclosure released Wednesday evening.
Wednesday’s filing covers dozens of independent expenditures made by Musk’s America PAC from Aug. 18 to Aug. 31, with two additional outlays planned for Sept. 10.
The majority of Musk’s spending — more than $700,000 — was concentrated on Senate Republicans’ races: He spent over $247,000 in Texas to support state Attorney General Ken Paxton, $170,000 for Maine Sen. Susan Collins and $105,000 for Ohio Sen. Jon Husted, with additional expenditures in New Hampshire, Iowa, Alaska and Michigan.
The super PAC also contributed nearly $90,000 to several House races. He dropped $37,500 on races involving Pennsylvania Reps. Scott Perry, Ryan Mackenzie and Rob Bresnahan and $11,000 on Rep. Tom Kean Jr.’s race in New Jersey. The super PAC also spent around $10,000 each to boost New York Rep. Mike Lawler and Wisconsin Rep. Derrick Van Orden, and the same amount against Rep. Jared Moskowitz (D-Florida).
Trending
Musk poured hundreds of millions into the 2024 presidential cycle, making him one of the country’s most influential political donors. While the Tesla founder indicated last May that he would be spending “a lot less” on political campaigns in the future, Musk has authorized his super PAC to spend up to $120 million on a new field program to help elect Republicans in November, The New York Times reported in July.
House Speaker Mike Johnson met with the tech billionaire in Texas last week, though the speaker declined to describe their conversation in detail.
“He’s made public a lot of what he’s doing,” Johnson said when CBS News asked if he expected Musk to contribute to the midterms. “I’m not going to talk about our conversation on that point, but we’re going to win the midterms.”
